source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 3. The following BIOS settings paths are from the Intel reference platform. Locations of these settings may be different on your BIOS implementation Customer Scripts (CScripts) Enabling The following is a quick reference of the key BIOS knobs for CScripts: • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > Lock Chipset = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration > MSR Lock Control = Disable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > IIO Configuration > DFX Global Configuration > — EV DFX Features = Enable — Disable BIOS Done = [X] ELOG Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > eMCA Settings > — EMCA Error Support= Enable — EMCA Logging Support= Enable — Corrected Error eLog = Enable — Memory Error eLog = Enable — Processor Error eLog = Enable Error Reporting Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > WHEA Settings > — WHEA Support = Enable — WHEA Log Memory Error = Enable — WHEA Log Processor Error = Enable — WHEA Log PCI Error = Enable Error Injection Enabling • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > — System Errors = Enable — System Memory Poison = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Error Injection Settings > — MCA Bank Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Injection Support = Enable — WHEA PCIe* Error Action Table = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > — IIO/PCH Global Error Support = Enable — IIO MCA Support = Disable — IIO eDPC Support = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe* Corrected Error Threshold Counter = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > PCIE Error Enabling > PCIe AER Corrected Errors = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > LMCE Support = Enable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Memory Error Enabling > Memory Corrected Error = Enable • EDKII > Socket Configuration > Uncore Configuration > Uncore General Configuration > Directory Mode Enable = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > Miscellaneous Configuration > Enable DAM Pin = Enable Firmware First Model • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > EMCA Settings > — EMCA Logging Support = Enable — EMCA CMCI-SMI Morphing = EMCA gen2 CSMI — EMCA CMCI-SMI Threshold = 0 — EMCA MCA-SMI Enable = EMCA gen 2 - MSMI • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > IIO Error Enabling > OS Native AER Support = Disable Crash Log • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > CPU CrashLog Feature = Disable • EDKII > Platform Configuration > System Event Log > Crash Log Enabling > PCH CrashLog Feature = Disable 4. Other OS Notes You can use grub2-mkconfig to specify "ras=cec_disable" by modifying /etc/default/grub's "GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX" with "ras=cec_disable". 【During Test】 1. Correctable Error on Primary Channel specific BIOS setup : • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > Memory RAS Configuration > — Mirror Mode = Full Mirror Mode • Socket Configuration > Memory Configuration > — Enforce Population POR = Disable • Disabling this knob is not required but was disabled because a non-POR memory population was used. It is highly recommended to have a POR memory population. 2. Halt and confirm there are no preexisting memory related errors on the system. Clear any found error logs or cold boot the system. >>> halt() >>> error.check_mem_errors() 3. Verify that mirroring is enabled by reading the following bit-field. >>> sv.socket0.soc.memss.b2cmi0.mode.mirror 4. Check that the memory configuration aligns with what is expected. Full memory mirroring, therefore, active memory capacity is equal to half the installed capacity; all channels are operating in mirror mode and the mirror size is equal to the active memory size. With the current CScripts version there were issues seen with the reported mirror size values but everything else aligns with expectations. >>> mc.dimminfoNoSPD() 5. Print the valid TAD arrays to check that they show they are mirrored. >>> mc.addTran() 6. Use the following command to translate how a few addresses, within the specified system address range, map to its physical DIMM address. Take note of the memory controller ("mc") column. From this table, system addresses can be selected to test injecting errors into mirrored regions on different memory controllers. >>> ras.mem.sa2da_table(0x100000000, 0x100000400, 64) 7. Check if the injectors are locked for all sockets and unlock if locked. >>> ei.utils.checkInjectorLock(and_unlock=True) 8. Choose the target device for error injection and modify masks for a single device correctable ECC error injection. >>> ei.mem.memDevs(dev0=1, dev0msk=0x3, dev1=2, dev1msk=0x0) 9. Inject and consume the correctable ECC error. >>> ei.mem.injectMemError(addr=0x000100000000, errType="ce", verbose=True) 10. Check that the target's IMC machine check bank has a correctable read error logged. The CScripts version used has some issues with its MC bank decoding features and manual decoding may be necessary if more information is desired. Checking that MSCOD == 0x80 is the key detail here. Note that the logged address is incorrect due to a sighting that will be fixed in a future stepping. >>> error.check_mem_errors(socket_id=0) >>> error.manualMcaDecode() 11. Resume the system to allow all error handling flows to complete. >>> go()

test_case.test_name: Correctable Error on Primary Channel — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Demonstrate that a correctable ECC fault injected into the primary side of a Full-Mirror GNR memory region is reported by the intended IMC as the expected correctable read error while mirror configuration remains healthy.
required_package: GNR/BIOS/BMC/OS and every DIMM PN/serial/slot/POR population
CScripts version/hash/license and documented mirror-size/logged-address sightings
Installed/active capacity, mirror bit, mirrored channels/TAD and primary-versus-mirror MC mapping
Approved sa2da result for address0x100000000 and exact memDevs semantics
Expected target IMC fields and MSCOD0x80 manual decoding
Dedicated window, cold-boot policy if needed and OOB recovery/restoration
test_case.test_command: Record DIMM/POR/full-mirror topology and harness limitations; preserve existing memory evidence; verify mirror bit, installed-versus-active half capacity, all-channel mirror state and TAD arrays; use the literal sa2da range to prove address0x100000000 maps to the intended primary MC/DIMM; unlock once, set the exact single-device masks and inject one CE; capture injector plus target IMC/manual MCA decoder MSCOD0x80, ignoring the known incorrect logged address for identity; go, collect platform logs/health and restore settings.
test_case.expected_result: Error is injected successfully. Error logs should match.

Stop on UCE, wrong IMC/MSCOD, hang or mirror degradation; no automatic retry/cold boot
Restore temporary POR/mirror/debug settings and verify memory/OS/BMC health
expected_evidence: Mirror bit, installed/active half capacity, channel/mirror/TAD outputs
sa2da address-to-primary-MC/DIMM proof and exact masks
One CE injector transcript and target IMC error check
Manual MCA decode with MSCOD0x80 and documented logged-address limitation
Post-go mirror/memory/OS/BMC health, restoration and engineer verdict
